sections.label: Government gambling stance
sections.summary: The Government does not encourage gambling but allows some forms in a controlled and safe environment, as total prohibition would drive gambling underground and cause more issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Government does not encourage gambling, but allows some forms of gambling in a controlled and safe environment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Total prohibition will drive gambling underground and cause more law-and-order and social issues.

sections.label: Singapore Pools online turnover growth
sections.summary: The percentage of online turnover for Singapore Pools' sports betting grew from 30% to 80% in the past five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The percentage of online turnover for Singapore Pools’ sports betting has grown in the past five years from 30% to 80%.

sections.label: Gambling Regulatory Authority of Singapore
sections.summary: Gambling legislation will be amended to establish the Gambling Regulatory Authority of Singapore as the single regulator for all forms of gambling.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To keep pace with this evolving gambling landscape, we will amend gambling legislation to establish the Gambling Regulatory Authority of Singapore, or GRA, as the single regulator for all forms of gambling.

sections.label: New licensing regime
sections.summary: The licensing regime will replace the various gambling permit and exemption regimes under today's gambling legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The licensing regime will replace the various gambling permit and exemption regimes under today’s gambling legislation.

sections.label: Licensing for private establishments
sections.summary: MHA will introduce a new licensing regime for gambling among members at private establishments, such as social clubs and clans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In particular, MHA will introduce a new licensing regime for gambling among members at private establishments, such as social clubs and clans.

sections.label: Class licence regime
sections.summary: Part 4 Division 2 introduces a class licence regime for GRA to regulate lower-risk gaming or gambling products, including mystery boxes, online games with gambling elements and business promotion lucky draws.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Part 4 Division 2 introduces a class licence regime for GRA to regulate lower-risk gaming or gambling products, including mystery boxes, online games with gambling elements and business promotion lucky draws.

sections.label: Exemption period for gambling services
sections.summary: Persons exempt under current laws can continue providing the gambling service for a fixed period of five to 12 months, instead of two to five months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Persons who are exempt under current laws can continue providing the gambling service for a fixed period of five to 12 months, instead of two to five months as stated.

sections.label: Minimum age for gambling
sections.summary: The minimum age for gambling remains 21, except at Singapore Pools' physical outlets where it remains 18, as set out in clause 13.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The minimum age for gambling will remain at 21 years old, except for gambling at Singapore Pools' physical outlets, which will remain at 18 years old, as set out in clause 13.

sections.label: Offences involving underaged gambling
sections.summary: Clauses 30, 34 and 35 criminalise gambling with underaged individuals, inducing them to gamble, and employing them to conduct gambling, except social physical gambling.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To better protect underaged persons, we will also criminalise gambling with underaged individuals, with the exception of social physical gambling, in clause 30; inducing underaged individuals to engage in gambling that is not social physical gambling in clause 34; and employing underaged individuals to conduct gambling in clause 35.

sections.label: Exclusion orders under clause 134
sections.summary: Clause 134 codifies current exemption or permit conditions to let NCPG issue exclusion orders barring persons from fruit machine rooms and Singapore Pools' online gambling products, besides casinos.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 134 codifies the current exemption or permit conditions in law, to allow NCPG to issue exclusion orders to persons to prevent them from entering fruit machine rooms and from betting on Singapore Pools' online gambling products, in addition to being excluded from the casinos.

sections.label: Advertising unlawful gambling offence
sections.summary: Clause 85 introduces an offence for advertising unlawful gambling, applying the current online threshold to physical gambling to address differing thresholds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This sets a higher bar and imposes enforcement difficulties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Hence, to address this difference in thresholds, clause 85 introduces an offence for advertising unlawful gambling where we will apply the threshold that we currently have for online, to physical gambling.

sections.label: Social gambling and private establishment licences
sections.summary: Social gambling among family and friends in homes is exempted, and private establishments with member gambling activities must apply for licences from the Gambling Regulatory Authority.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Second, we will exempt social gambling amongst family and friends in homes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Lastly, private establishments with gambling activities for their members will be required to apply for licences from the Gambling Regulatory Authority.

sections.label: Expanding CRA to form GRA
sections.summary: The CRA is proposed to be expanded to form GRA as a single regulator for all gambling, pooling government resources and expertise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: These are CRA, the Gambling Regulatory Unit in MHA headquarters, the Singapore Totalisator Board, the Police and MSF.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: We propose to expand the CRA today to form GRA as the single regulator for all forms of gambling, to pool and optimise resources and expertise across the Government.

sections.label: GRA functions under Clause 5
sections.summary: Clause 5 sets out GRA's functions: regulating gambling honestly and free from criminal influence, fostering responsible gambling, and maintaining standards and accountability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 5 outlines GRA's functions, which include regulating gambling activities in or affecting Singapore to ensure that it is conducted honestly and free from criminal influence and exploitation; fostering responsible gambling and minimising harms caused by gambling; and setting and maintaining standards and accountability for the conduct of gambling.

sections.label: Exclusion by Law for tenants
sections.summary: From 1 June 2022, Exclusion by Law will extend to all tenants and occupiers in the Public Rental Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: From 1 June 2022, Exclusion by Law will extend to all tenants and occupiers in the Public Rental Scheme.

sections.label: Notice to newly excluded persons
sections.summary: A question asks how the Minister will ensure appropriate notice is given to individuals newly categorised as excluded persons from 1 June 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given that a significant number of new individuals will be subject to the Exclusion of Law come 1 June 2022, can Minister share how he will ensure that appropriate notice is given to individuals newly categorised as excluded persons?

sections.label: Offence of underaged inducement
sections.summary: Under the new section 34, it would be an offence to send an underaged individual an inducement to gamble.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the new section 34, it would be an offence to send an underaged individual an inducement to gamble.

sections.label: Police entry bans on individuals
sections.summary: The Commissioner for Police may impose entry bans if an individual's criminal history presents an unacceptable risk to gambling service integrity standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Commissioner for Police may impose entry bans on an individual if they deem that the individual's criminal history will present an unacceptable risk to maintaining proper standards of integrity of any gambling service.

sections.label: NCPG 2020 gambling survey findings
sections.summary: The NCPG's 2020 survey found almost half of Singapore residents aged 18 and above gamble, with 6% reporting lack of self-control.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The National Council for Problem Gambling (NCPG)'s 2020 survey found that almost half of Singapore residents aged 18 and above participate in gambling activities, with 6% reporting that they lack self-control when gambling.

sections.label: Casinos and gambling expansion
sections.summary: Two casinos opened in 2010, and in 2019 the Government raised the slot machine cap and increased gambling floorspace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Two casinos were opened in 2010 and in 2019, the Government raised the cap on the number of slot machines allowed and increased the floorspace allocated to gambling.

sections.label: First gambling experience ages
sections.summary: The NCPG survey found 35% of Singapore residents first gambled between ages 18 and 24, the highest among all age groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The NCPG survey similarly found that 35% of Singapore residents had their first gambling experience between the ages of 18 and 24, the highest among all age groups.

sections.label: UK children loot box purchases
sections.summary: UK research found that of the 93% of children who play video games, 25% to 40% have made loot box purchases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Research from the UK has found that of the 93% of children who play video games, 25% to 40% have made loot box purchases.

sections.label: Gambling Control Bill education question
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Gambling Control Bill will bring greater educational efforts to discourage Singaporeans, particularly young people, from gambling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With the introduction of the Gambling Control Bill, will there be greater educational efforts to discourage Singaporeans, particularly young people, from participating in gambling activities and delaying their first gambling experience?

sections.label: Loot box education effectiveness question
sections.summary: The question asks whether such educational efforts have been found to genuinely reduce loot box use among youths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Have such educational efforts been found to genuinely reduce loot box use among youths?

sections.label: Call against social gambling
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to reassess social gambling and on Parliament to take a stronger stance against gambling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In summary, I would like to call on the Government to reassess its position on social gambling and to take a strong stand against gambling by children, especially in the area of loot boxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: More generally, I call on Parliament to take a stronger stance against gambling.

sections.label: Unified Gambling Regulatory Authority
sections.summary: Reconstituting the Casino Regulatory Authority with other agencies into a single Gambling Regulatory Authority consolidates resources for a holistic approach to gambling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The reconstitution of the Casino Regulatory Authority with the rationalisation and consolidation of other Government agencies, such as the Gambling Regulatory Unit, Singapore Tote Board, departments within the Police and MSF that are addressing social gambling problems to establish a single unified Gambling Regulatory Authority is an important step of consolidating resources to address gambling, not just from narrow, segregated lenses, but taking a holistic approach to gambling policies and issues.

sections.label: Proxy gambling offence safeguards
sections.summary: The speaker asks what safeguards ensure casino licensees help enforce the proxy gambling ban and what penalties apply if they are negligent or abetting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Next, I note the new offence of proxy gambling, which I understand was to close a loophole where there was a case in 2019 in which the individuals could not be taken to task as proxy gambling was not previously criminalised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What safeguards and regulations are being rolled out to ensure that the two casino licensees are proactively assisting the Government to enforce the ban on proxy gambling and what penalties could be imposed if they are found to be negligent or even abetting such practices?

sections.label: 2020 gambling participation survey
sections.summary: A 2020 National Council on Problem Gambling survey found 44% of Singapore residents aged 18 and above gambled in the past year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   According to the National Council on Problem Gambling survey on Singaporeans' participation in gambling in 2020, 44% of Singapore residents aged 18 and above have participated in at least one type of gambling activity in the past year.

sections.label: Problem gambling social protection
sections.summary: The speaker says resources must strengthen social protection against problem gambling, notes home mahjong is not illegal, and hopes families get more support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even as we restructure the CRA into a new GRA to strengthen the regulatory framework for gambling, we must also look squarely at the issue of problem gambling and continue to invest additional resources to strengthen social protection against problem gambling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Bill also clearly states that it is not illegal for friends and relatives to play mahjong at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I understand that the police will crack down on any syndicate that takes the advantage to engage in illegal gambling activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, I also hope that we can provide more support and protection for families that need help, to prevent their family member from turning to problem gambling or pathological gambling from social gambling.

sections.label: Consolidating gambling regulation bodies
sections.summary: The speaker supports consolidating regulation bodies under a single Gambling Regulatory Authority to regulate all forms of gambling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The constant stream of unsolicited text messages touting illegal betting activities comes to mind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I support the consolidation of regulation bodies under a single Gambling Regulatory Authority (GRA) to regulate all forms of gambling activities.

sections.label: Cross-border remote gambling consolidation
sections.summary: Asks how consolidating gambling control measures will affect management of cross-border remote gambling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, how will the consolidation of gambling control measures impact the management of cross-border remote gambling?

sections.label: Excluded financial risk products
sections.summary: Asks the Ministry to clarify which products and services with financial risk elements are being excluded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Third, can the Ministry provide further clarification on products and services containing financial risk elements, which are being excluded?

sections.label: Advertising laws and mystery boxes
sections.summary: Asks how updated advertising and promotion laws apply to activities with optional gambling elements, including mobile games with mystery boxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Lastly, how will the updated Advertising and Promotion (A&P) laws apply to activities containing an optional gambling element, including mobile games with mystery boxes?

sections.label: Minimum gambling age 21
sections.summary: The Bill sets the minimum age for legal gambling at 21 years old, one of the highest internationally.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: In the Bill, the minimum age for legal gambling is set at 21 years old, one of the highest internationally.

sections.label: Exclusion of public rental tenants
sections.summary: Removes the six-month rental arrears requirement for excluding public rental tenants and occupiers from gambling, impacting about 4,000 individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Currently, undischarged bankrupts, those receiving ComCare – Short-to-Medium-Term and Long-Term assistance, those on legal aid and tenants of the HDB's public rental scheme with six or more months of rental arrears are already excluded from casinos, fruit machine rooms and Singapore Pools' online gambling.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: To strengthen upstream protection for public rental tenants and occupiers, we are removing the need to accumulate six months of rental arrears before they are excluded by law.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Most individuals residing in public rental housing do not visit the casinos, fruit machine rooms or have an online gambling account with Singapore Pools.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: However, a small fraction of about 4,000 individuals residing in public rental housing, who engaged in at least one of these gambling activities will be impacted.

sections.label: NCPG letters to households
sections.summary: All public rental households will receive a letter from NCPG with an infographic about the June extension of Exclusion by Law.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: For the extension of Exclusion by Law to all public rental tenants and occupiers in June later this year, all public rental households will receive a letter from NCPG, together with an infographic, to inform them of this change.

sections.label: Mandatory responsible gambling requirements
sections.summary: MSF and the new Gambling Regulatory Authority will make responsible gambling requirements mandatory for fruit machine rooms, complementing a regime that cut rooms from 61 in 2017 to 46 in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: To emphasise the importance of responsible gambling and to ensure a baseline standard of responsible gambling across fruit machine rooms, MSF and the new Gambling Regulatory Authority will be making responsible gambling requirements mandatory.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: These requirements include educating patrons on problem gambling and how to gamble responsibly, informing patrons of the NCPG helpline number and help services and ensuring fruit machine room staff are trained to assist patrons who display signs of problem gambling.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: This change complements the Government's tightening of the fruit machine room regime over the years which resulted in the number of fruit machine rooms reducing by about 25%, from 61 in 2017 to 46 in 2021.

sections.label: Loot box education efforts
sections.summary: The NCPG has stepped up efforts to educate youth, parents, educators and the public on the potential connection between loot boxes and gambling.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: To Mr Gerald Giam's query on teaching students about the ills of loot boxes, the NCPG has stepped up efforts to educate youth, parents, educators and the public on the potential connection between loot boxes and gambling.

sections.label: Social gambling at home only
sections.summary: Social gambling will only be allowed in a person's home, not in places like hotels and chalets, since covering non-residential places could be exploited by criminal elements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Social gambling will only be allowed in a person's home and will not be allowed in places like hotels and chalets, which Mr Louis Chua was asking about, and since covering non-residential places under the exemption could be exploited by criminal elements.

sections.label: Blocking illegal online gambling
sections.summary: A key part of the strategy to combat illegal online gambling is blocking illegal online gambling websites, advertisements accessible in Singapore, and linked payment services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: A key part of our strategy to combat illegal online gambling is our blocking measures for illegal online gambling websites as well as advertisements that can be accessed in Singapore, as well as the payment services that are linked to illegal online gambling.

sections.label: Inducement to gamble strict liability
sections.summary: The offence of inducement to gamble in clause 34 has strict liability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: The offence of inducement to gamble in clause 34 has strict liability.

sections.label: Chance-based loot boxes not gambling
sections.summary: Current laws and regulations do not consider chance-based loot boxes as gambling as long as there are no in-game monetisation facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Currently, our laws and regulations do not consider chance-based loot boxes as gambling as long as there are no in-game monetisation facilities.

sections.label: Online games advertisement restriction review
sections.summary: A blanket restriction on advertising online games is not practical, and the landscape of online games of chance will be reviewed, including regulating advertisements of those falling under the Gambling Control Bill's gambling definition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: We agree with Mr Yip Hon Weng that a blanket restriction on the advertisement of online games would not be practical, especially since these games are perceived by many as leisure and entertainment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: We will be reviewing the landscape of online games of chance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: This will include how to regulate advertisements of online games of chance that fall in the definition of gambling under the Gambling Control Bill.

sections.label: GRA resource neutral establishment
sections.summary: The establishment of GRA will be resource neutral across the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: The establishment of GRA will be resource neutral across the Government.

sections.label: GRA oversight of regulatory regimes
sections.summary: GRA will oversee existing regulatory regimes and new ones, such as licensing for gambling in private establishments and class-licence regimes for low-risk gambling products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: In addition to overseeing existing regulatory regimes, GRA will also oversee new regulatory regimes, such as the new licensing regime for gambling in private establishments and class-licence regimes for low-risk gambling products.

sections.label: Social gambling in homes conditions
sections.summary: There is no minimum age for social gambling within homes, which is to be put under an exemption regime with conditions: it must happen in a home, within a family and friends context, and with no financial gains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: The first question, the answer is yes, there is no minimum age for social gambling within homes and that is the reason why we have mentioned that we wanted to put social gambling under the exemption regime precisely, and also to state the conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: One, is that it has to happen in a home and not outside of the home; secondly, it has to happen within the context of a family, as well as friends, people acquainted with each other; and thirdly, there ought to be no gains, financial gains, from this social gambling.

sections.label: NCPG youth anti-gambling messaging
sections.summary: NCPG cited Wang Lei's Chinese New Year advertisements and a CNA documentary on loot boxes, and will continue messaging to tell youth not to get started with gambling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I am sure you remember during the Chinese New Year period, we had Wang Lei on various YouTube advertisements and advertisements on TV as well, espousing the messages of, "Are you still gambling right now?" That was in Mandarin, by the way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: And specifically to youths, the message is Be Smart, Don't Start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: And I cited the example of the CNA documentary series earlier about loot boxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: So that is the position of NCPG and they will continue working on the messaging for telling youth not to get started with gambling, and that is the key message and they will keep going at it.
